market_question: Will Renan Santos finish in second place in the first round of the 2026 Brazilian presidential election?
reasoning: Renan Santos is a minor left-wing politician with negligible national recognition. In 2022, PSOL's far better-known candidate Guilherme Boulos received only 6.9% and did not finish second. Major centrist and right-wing figures (e.g., Lula, possible PL candidate) will likely occupy the top two spots, leaving virtually no chance for Santos to be the runner-up.
evidence_points: Renan Santos is leader of PSOL but has no broad national polling presence.
In 2022, PSOL candidate Boulos got 6.9% and placed 4th, far behind the top two (Lula ~48%, Bolsonaro ~43%).
Bolsonaro's ineligibility could strengthen an alternative right candidate, further dimming a PSOL runner-up scenario.
The first round typically sees two polarized candidates; a left-wing second-place finish behind Lula would go to a more established figure.
sources_consulted: Polling data from Datafolha and Ipec (2023-2025)
